content:
Google released the all-new Pixel 11 series earlier this month. Compared to last year's Pixel 10, the new models don't see major spec changes, but they bring several welcome experience improvements. One of them is a new camera processing option that gives you significantly more control over the final look of your photos.

With the iPhone 18 Pro on the horizon, I hope Apple will follow suit.

Pixel 11 introduces a camera feature called Camera Looks, which is somewhat similar to Photographic Styles on iPhone, letting you adjust how your camera renders its shots. These adjustments are made before image capture, so it's not just a regular filter.

Google offers multiple presets that echo Apple's styles, plus fine-grained adjustment for each one. Beyond that, there are several new choices that tap into a new wave of mobile photography trends: Editorial, Velvet, Classic, Digi, Black Tie, and Minimal.

These styles all step away from the heavy post-processing look that's typical of smartphone photos, trying to recapture the spirit of old-school photography. Digi, as the name suggests, pursues the low dynamic range, high contrast, and high noise texture of small-sensor point-and-shoot cameras from the 2010s.

Minimal, meanwhile, goes the opposite direction, emphasizing minimal-processing, natural rendering. A lot of the HDR processing pipeline simply doesn't run, and you see more or less exactly what your smartphone sensor captured. You can see some sample photos on 9to5Google.

With ProRAW on iPhone, you could theoretically revert a photo back to a state that looks barely processed, but doing so kind of defeats the purpose of smartphone photography in the first place.

Wrap-up

If Apple wants to build the truly best pocket camera, it needs to understand that not every user is chasing the same look. Photographic Styles is a good start, but Apple should go further. Photography is, after all, a form of self-expression, so giving users more options to control how much processing their photos receive is the right call. Apple should take a page from Google and add a 'Minimal' style to iPhone.

What do you think about the state of iPhone photography? Do you like Apple's recent Photographic Styles, or do you think they still fall short? Drop your thoughts in the comments.
